gen-fs-rx-100-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega draws every letter with one nib and a visible gap in each c, while RX100 packs itself above it in tight, crowded rows. The pair's strongest quality is that tension between cramped and spread.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-lexend-peta: Tight, futuristic, and stiff as stencil metal. RX100 crowds its letters into a dense, tall-bodied block, and Lexend Peta, a sans-serif with wide-mouthed c shapes and unthinned curves, lets the page loosen up beneath it.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-lexend-tera: Zero stroke modulation is RX100's signature, each letter squeezed tight against the next with a towering x-height. Lexend Tera does the opposite job, spacing its plotter-pen lines like stepping stones so the open curves can be read one by one.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-lexend-zetta: Approachable is the first word for the body here, yet RX100 above it is all crowded, futuristic compression with a dominant x-height. Lexend Zetta takes the other job, stretching its ribbon-like, widely tracked letters out so each one gets room.
gen-fs-rx-100-gf-montserrat-alternates: RX100 is jammed, monoline and futuristic, its tall lowercase pressed shoulder to shoulder across the line. Montserrat Alternates, a plain sans, simply opens up, with a paperclip-wide c.
gen-fs-segment-gf-cascadia-code: Systematic is the word for Segment, which spaces its tall, stocky letters far apart, and Cascadia Code takes up that wide spacing too. Through a longer passage the thin, neon-tube lines would glide along smoothly.
gen-fs-segment-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads like a plain sans with its letters standing apart like pins in a wide board, compact and uniform in height. And Segment, with its stocky middle band and breathing counters, makes it feel like a louder sibling.
gen-fs-segment-gf-julius-sans-one: Segment's tall middle band makes its lines look stocky, with plenty of space between letters and open counters inside. Julius Sans One does the opposite, whispering with barely any gap between capital and lowercase height.
gen-fs-segment-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads with a big x-height, wide curves that stay distinct, and short stubby ascenders and descenders. Segment hits hard with its stocky tall middle band, while the body sans holds its wire-thin line.
gen-fs-segment-gf-lexend-giga: Stocky and spaced out, Segment fills its big letters with open counters, while Lexend Giga sits below as a plain sans with flat, single-weight linework. Both give each word generous room, which makes them feel like cousins.
